title: Latency rollups & dashboards per endpoint / model / region (p95 & p99 + tokens/sec normalization)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add aggregated latency signals (p50/p95/p99) and tokens-per-second normalized throughput metrics surfaced in the Console per endpoint (route), model, and region. Goals: 1) make regressions obvious to owners by showing percentile rollups + trendlines and tokens/sec normalized baselines; 2) connect load-test results and production SLI snapshots to the same dashboards for easier regression triage; 3) enable automated regression detection alerts that can create a ticket and attach the failing harness run.
background: Current observability exposes overall latency SLOs and some route-level p95s but lacks a consistent per-endpoint+model+region view that ties in tokens/sec and load-harness data. Engineers spend time correlating separate charts and running ad-hoc queries when investigating latency regressions after model rollouts or infra changes.
proposal_summary: Implement backend rollup pipelines to compute p50/p95/p99 over configurable windows (1m, 5m, 1h) partitioned by endpoint, model_version, and region. Augment metrics with tokens/sec and normalized latency (latency per 100 tokens) and show them in new Console panels. Add an automated regression detector that compares current percentiles to historical baselines and posts findings to a Slack channel and optionally opens a Linear ticket with links to the failing load-test run.
acceptance_criteria: New Console dashboard exists at Observability -> Latency by Surface with filters for endpoint, model, region, and model_version
Percentiles (p50/p95/p99) compute correctly from production telemetry for 1m/5m/1h windows and match runbook query examples
Tokens/sec and normalized latency (ms per 100 tokens) displayed alongside percentiles
Load-test harness produces a structured run artifact that can be linked from the dashboard
Regression detector flags deviations >= 20% in p95 or p99 relative to a rolling 30d baseline and opens a pre-filled Linear draft with context
Performance queries run within existing metrics latency budget and do not increase Prometheus/metrics storage costs materially (use rollup jobs / sampling)
Unit and integration tests for the aggregation job and regression detector exist and pass in CI
implementation_notes: Add aggregation worker that consumes request spans and token-count annotations from the event stream; compute approximate histograms per partition using HDR histograms
Store rollups in a new timeseries namespace 'rdw.latency_rollups' with labels: endpoint, model, model_version, region, window
Expose tokens/sec as a derived metric computed from token_count / request_duration aggregated over window
Build new Console components: a pivoted table (rows=endpoint, cols=region) and an overlay heatmap for model versions
Regression detector service runs daily and on-demand; it compares the latest 1h p99/p95 to a 30-day smoothed baseline using EWMA; alarms created when breach persists for 3 consecutive windows
Integration points: load-harness (link runs), github PR status (attach perf diff), Slack channel #perf-alerts
Roll forward strategy: default to read-only dashboards first, then enable automated alerts after 1 week of observation
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: Ticket created by Asha. Drafted acceptance criteria and initial design; assigned to Tom.
2026-03-02: Spike completed. Validated HDR histograms approach on 10k requests/sec stream; memory footprint acceptable. Prototype rollup worker implemented in go-worker branch 'latency-rollups'.
2026-03-04: Console design sync with UX. Decided on pivot table + heatmap + time-series trendline. Design PR: https://drive.example.com/designs/latency-rollups (placeholder).

2026-03-05: Integration plan with load-harness defined. Harness will publish a run JSON to S3 with tags (endpoint, model, region, commit). Regression detector can fetch run artifacts to attach evidence.
testing_plan: Unit tests for rollup worker (synthetic histograms, edge cases: zero tokens, outliers)
Integration test: end-to-end ingest -> rollup -> Console panel rendering in staging with synthetic traffic
Load-test: run existing harness (ENG-7316) against dedicated staging stack to validate aggregation correctness at 20k tokens/sec
Regression simulation: replay historic production traces with injected latency shifts to verify detector sensitivity and false-positive rate
rollout_plan: Stage 1: deploy rollup worker to staging and seed dashboards with historical 30d data. Stage 2: enable dashboards in read-only mode for a single team (Serving Runtime) for 3 days. Stage 3: enable regression alerts for that team with 24/7 notify=false (no paging) for 7 days. Stage 4: enable automated ticket creation and expand to all teams. Revert plan: disable detector and purge new rollups if we observe metric explosion or incorrect aggregations.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on histogram truncation strategy and memory bounds for high-cardinality partitions
Validate the detector threshold heuristic (20% by default) and propose adjustments for low-traffic endpoints
We will need SRE sign-off on storage knobs before enabling alerts in prod
estimated_cost_notes: Estimated infra cost: small increase in TSDB storage for rolled-up metrics; we anticipate offsetting by using downsampled windows and retention rules
final_notes: This ticket ties load-test outputs to the primary observability surface for latency. It should drastically reduce time-to-detect and time-to-triage for regressions after model or infra changes.
